plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Master Services Agreement of this type almost always carries a limitation of liability article. Scan the full body for headings such as 'Limitation of Liability', 'Liability', or damages exclusions and check the cap is mutual, tied to fees paid, and carves out IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach and willful misconduct.

Expect an indemnification article later in the unexposed body. Verify Kubient indemnifies AP for third-party IP infringement, breach of confidentiality/data obligations and its negligence or willful misconduct, and that any AP-side indemnity is narrow (limited to AP-supplied content/materials). If no such clause exists in the full text, propose insertion.

No covenant or restrictive-covenant heading appears in the outline; non-competes binding a media customer are rare in ad-tech services agreements. Confirm by scanning for 'Non-Compete', 'Restrictive Covenants', 'Competing Services' or restrictions embedded in an exclusivity/term clause before concluding absence.

No exclusivity heading is visible. Still check the services/scope and term provisions for 'sole and exclusive', 'exclusive provider' or preferred-supplier language that would limit AP's ability to use other demand or supply partners.

No pricing or fees section is exposed. Look in any fees/compensation or schedule provisions for 'most favoured', 'no less favourable', or best-terms language; flag only if the obligation runs against AP (MFN in our favour is acceptable).

Not visible in the outline. Check general/miscellaneous provisions and any personnel or confidentiality clause for hiring restrictions; if present and binding AP, require mutuality, a 12-month cap and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

'Initial Term' is a defined term, so a term-and-termination article exists in the unexposed body. Confirm AP may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice without penalty or early-termination fee, and that Kubient has no symmetrical mid-term walk-away right.

The defined 'Initial Term' points to a term clause with likely renewal mechanics. Check for automatic renewal, the length of any non-renewal notice window (target 30 days or less) and whether renewal pricing increases are capped.

Governing law and venue normally sit in the miscellaneous provisions at the end of the agreement, outside the exposed preamble. Verify New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales law with court jurisdiction rather than arbitration; the preamble's recital of Kubient's offices may hint at the chosen forum.

Expect an assignment clause among the general provisions. Confirm AP may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that Kubient cannot terminate on an AP change of control.

An intellectual property / data ownership article should appear in the body. Confirm AP retains ownership of its content, inventory data and any deliverables paid for, and that Kubient receives only a limited service-delivery licence with no assignment of AP IP or aggregated-data rights.

Look for the licence grant in the services/platform access provisions of the unexposed body. Ensure the grant to AP extends to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and is not revocable at Kubient's discretion outside a termination event.

Audit or records-inspection language may appear in the fees or compliance provisions. If Kubient has audit rights over AP, limit to once annually, 10 business days' notice, business hours, remote/off-site where possible, at Kubient's cost, subject to AP confidentiality and security rules.

No fees or remedies section is exposed. Scan payment, term and SLA provisions for liquidated damages, early-termination fees or penalty language payable by AP; service credits running to AP are acceptable.

Expect a representations and warranties article, possibly followed by a disclaimer. Confirm Kubient warrants performance in a professional manner and conformity to specifications for a meaningful period with re-performance or refund as the remedy, and that any 'AS IS' disclaimer does not gut it.

Insurance covenants are frequently omitted from ad-tech master services agreements and none is visible in the outline. Confirm by scanning the general provisions and any exhibit/schedule; if absent, propose commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O and cyber cover with AP as additional insured where applicable.

No fees or order-form section is exposed. Check the payment/fees provisions and any schedule for minimum spend, minimum volume or take-or-pay commitments binding AP; if present, seek removal or an exit right on notice.

Transition assistance is often missing from vendor-drafted MSAs. Review the effect-of-termination and data provisions in the full text; if there is no obligation to return or delete AP data and provide reasonable wind-down assistance, propose adding a transition and data-return clause.
